subject.title: [Bug]: /context detail shows ~62k untracked provider/runtime overhead on fresh OpenAI Codex gpt-5.5 session

question: Should `/context detail` grow a provider-aware Codex ledger, or keep the current generic residual until live Codex semantics are proven?
rationale: The code can show additional buckets, but the correct user-facing semantics for cache, native thread state, hidden provider state, billing, and compaction pressure require maintainer intent plus live Codex evidence.

options.title: Add provider-aware ledger
options.body: Implement the ledger behind `/context detail`, backed by live Codex proof and tests that distinguish cached input, current context occupancy, known OpenClaw prompt sections, and unknown residual.

options.title: Document generic residual
options.body: Keep the current output shape and clarify that the residual is intentionally unknown provider/runtime state until Codex exposes stronger attribution.

options.title: Wait for upstream evidence
options.body: Leave the issue open without implementation until a maintainer or reporter provides a current-main Codex OAuth run that identifies the residual source.

recommendation.title: Add provider-aware ledger
recommendation.body: Implement the ledger behind `/context detail`, backed by live Codex proof and tests that distinguish cached input, current context occupancy, known OpenClaw prompt sections, and unknown residual.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the broadest adjacent history across context reporting and session usage accounting, where the product semantics would need to be set before implementation.
